This game seemed really fun, but turned out to be really repetitive. The variety of different planets and different conditions that can affect a planet (e.g. "entry fee is 50% of normal, but the price graph is upside down) is very low, so by the end of third campaign you will see everything the game gets to offer. There is buying stocks, selling stocks, shorting and "side betting" (i,e placing a bet that a random event chosen by game will happen or not). There are also consultants that you can hire. They provide you additional info that will help betting and trading. And that is... all. Well, each campaign after first two has it own gimmick, but they but almost no adjustments to playstyle is needed for any of them. On the campaigns, there are 6 of them. I got Gold medal on every campaign except for first and last ones, and basically used the same strategy in every single one of them. The first one is tricky because not all tools are unlocked to you from the start, and the last one requires a little bit of luck with side bets that I don't feel like grinding for. All planets feel more or less similar. There are 8 planets, but I felt like there are only two patterns of how price graphs can behave (constant up-down swings and steady up with a huge drop at the end). So, naturally, you develop a winning strategy by the end of the first hour of playing and sweep all the campaigns. In the end, 4 gold medals, 2 silver medals, 82% of achievements in 3 hours. Devs promise 4 more campaigns and a new mode in the future, but as it stands right now this game is really short, its idea becomes stale quickly ("short the baby" for the first time - hilarious, "short the baby" for 100th time - boring) and requires almost no challenge. Cannot say I recommend it.

Worse than the original (SWOTS) in every way. Can go on and on: 1) This game is 90% RNG. Only two choices matter; planet and baby. Each planet has "trends": Sequa Lux, Gooble Gibby peak early before crashing later, so on. Babies don't have any modifiers themselves (more on that in 2) rather they're a possible life on that planet. - You can plan better with consultants... sometimes they'll lie, othertimes they make you believe it's higher than actuality (happens fairly often) - Initially I wrote off side bets but it's evident they are a necessity for certain campaigns. Of course that too is RNG-dependent. Short/long positions are the only ones you can reasonably predict with consultants (even positions aren't guranteed to show up). - Shorting gimmick is meant to be the selling point but shorting can and will ruin your run. Even if you plan accordingly. Only reliable strat is after two steep negatives (even that isn't guranteed) - Very inconsistent difficulty curve. Some are piss easy. Some you can't even get silver on without RNG/side bets. - The scenario mode is a (somehow) more lackluster version of campaigns. Dailies are randomized rulesets + you can't savescum (almost a necessity with this game). 2) The story generation gimmick is very barebones - Events that shouldn't repeat do. Had a baby marry his childhood sweetheart twice. There was no "divorce" event that happened between the marriages. Dev claimed it's intentional to imply polyamory but it happens with similar events too. The game doesn't keep track of any additional characters the baby interacts with (family, friends, etc) so milestones like marriage and/or having kids is treated the same as gossiping in a grocery store or dancing in the rain. - Age isn't taken into consideration (oftentimes). A baby can get promoted at his parent's company at age 8, or promoted at an older age where he should have inherited the company by then. - Events that should leave a bigger impact on a life don't. This is best demonstrated in a clip the developers posted on their social media ([url=https://bsky.app/profile/strangescaffold.bsky.social/post/3mcd4fj64qk26]here[/url]). The baby they're playing had a drug problem at 16 that was never brought up again. One pointed this out (1:19). - babies have no stats beyond name and species (which doesn't affect anything). There's no real modifiers like sex/gender, background, family history, etc. So every baby plays exactly the same. In contrast SWOTS had five stats for organs; type, size, condition, blood type, and rarity. Some organs had special effects like changing the size and quality of other organs. - To add: Sequa Lux's description states that high net worth grants citizenship, except the game doesn't take status into consideration so it treats every baby the same way. A baby will be treated like a citizen one moment and a vagrant the next. - Events that shouldn't be lethal can be. One baby died from hearing loss. Another died from getting sued (you can infer suicide but game doesn't make mention of it) 3) Almost nonexistent story. - [spoiler]The FutureSee terminals are stupid. Who made them? One guy, a company? Why? How? Who knows. The tech solved many problems (war, advanced medicine, etc... even though war and disease prop up quite often in events...) but also killed speculative markets. If the elite are as corrupt as we're led to believe why don't they just seize/destroy this tech? Why are commonfolk allowed to use it for cheap???[/spoiler] Can go on and on how this set up doesn't make sense. Renders most of SWOTS worthless here (there's 0 mention of space warlords!) - Pretty much every campaign is just variation of "guy gets rich". I hoped this issue was limited to the first two campaigns. Nope every campaign is like this. The second campaign (Mr. Zip It) was originally going to involve Mr. Zip It shooting a god point blank to save a galaxy but it was scrapped being "too big a jump" from the first one. How come every campaign that follows his is equally underwhelming? - The little story you're given are through these news anchor bits that *sometimes* talks about the campaign. Often he'll just talk about irrelevant events. So the campaigns are just "character has dilemma", and the ending is "character doesn't have dilemma, also he's rich now". There's nothing in-between to make it interesting. (campaign that suffers the most from this is Pixem's; his is based off Falling Down but I didn't get that impression at all (apart from Pixem's glasses vaguely resembling D-Fen's)) - Finale is underwhelming (like the game itself!); [spoiler]At the end of Wengrave Shup's campaign you're thrown into a confrontation between her and this scientist guy. No build up, anticipation, it just happens.[/spoiler] Maybe cutscenes could've fixed this. 4) The graphical style is competent, but not great. - The aliens are samey, even with different faces they all share the same humanoid body. They're more like people wearing masks. Not saying they can't be humanoid. You can be creative with that restriction. But, they all share the same body regardless of species. - The babies themselves are odd. Same problem with the aliens, they all look the same, just different heads. You'd imagine insectoid baby to be a grub or caterpillar or something. The only "out-there" option is the "Flatwing" which is a grown buff guy (for some reason). Except they also look identical. They could've used other breakfast pastry like waffles, french toast, crossaints... - Don't get the point of giving babies different models and sprite icons if no variants exist like color, shape, etc etc. The "Flatwing" I mentioned earlier can only be pancakes. None that have waffle, french toast, or crossaint heads. - the new music is passable but nowhere near as good as organ sim's. Like the composer is trying to mimick RJ Lake best as he can but just can't. - SWOTS limited the color palette to reds and greens (some purples); this changed to blue and red but also rendering the babies in color and the cutscenes are in this painted style. Older sprites (cartoony, silly) at odds with new sprites (more detailed, realistic). (admittedly the robot baby is pretty funny) 5) Developer troubles... - This game had some drama (both Discord and Twitter) pre-release. I won't delve into it too much. Scaffold had high hopes for this game and really didn't like hearing people say otherwise. Critics were met with passive aggression (both from devs and fans). Devs tried to say the game being unfair was the player's fault (not the heavy RNG) - Feels unfinished. There were 8 campaigns in the demo, in the full game there was only 6. Just abruptly ends after Wengrave. You can complete the game in 2 - 3 hours. They try to lampshade it by presenting it as "new content" for free updates, it's obvious there was meant to be 8 campaigns in the final game. Feels like a excuse to release a unfinished game. Leads into the next point... - Game's running worse with every update. It ran fine at release, now lags horribly when I stream it to friends. - Scaffold has a bad habit of abandoning games way too early. Before this one they put out three other games which (iirc) were updated once or twice before being abandoned entirely. They'd get maybe one or two people talking about it before the channels died off. Expect this game to meet the same fate The positive reception this game is getting is baffling. This is NOT worth 20$ and the fact they're trying to charge 35$ for this in bundles borders on robbery. Just get SWOTS on sale. Or you want a stock trading game that's actually good? Get Insider Trading. EDIT: so the developers permanently banned me from the forum (day after this was written)([url=https://i.postimg.cc/Y998VwXh/29FFHA.png]proof[/url]) and blocked me from their Patreon (how i got the code)... I posted once (a month ago) nothing else. Can only assume this review (+ being top-rated) is what provoked it. Pretty scummy if true...

This game was a terrible dissapointment, sadly not only did it fail to meet the bar the previous title set, but actually failed to leave the ground. First thing first: The game looks wonderful, the thematics are good, the story telling is what I'd expect from this universe, all-in-all, the theme of the game feels great. But the gameplay is, very nothing sadly... There is 0 incentive to make money first off. Yes money is how you win, but it's basically a highscore, not actually money at that point. You have nothing to do with money other than dump it on stocks or put it in gambling. Because gambling doesn't actually cost money up front, nothing stops you from doing both, so any interesting resource management there is already diminished. The game is also just, effectively a mobile game, the only goal is to get gold rating on 6 levels then you're done. If you're like me and don't care about getting top scores, this game will be even worse for you, ignoring the other problems. Then you get the level/campaign/character design, which is, aggravting. For instance there is one character who just, loses access to betting. Does he get anything in return? some special feature? No he just don't have access to betting, which is like 33% of your money making options gone. You also have a character who's a market regulator, you'd expect his gimmick to be that he can rig the market? NOPE! He simply trades extremely slowly because he goes through a proxy. Another character just loses access to his consultants for part of his campaign. And while all these mechanics are fine *in theory* if they compensated you with neat skill/effects or buffs, no they all hurt you and/or remove decision making, in pursuit of making the game harder. The only character who felt fine was the sixth character, who, without spoilers, doesn't actually lose any decisions, and is probably the only character who is actually compensated for their negatives by having good consultants. Notice how I said 'fine', not good, fine. This is what I'd expect a basic character to be like, not end-game. Characters need to have some gimmick that makes you excited to play them, not some restriction that makes you never want to play them again. This game is almost entirely carried by it's consultant system. Consultants are fun, and their characters are charming, and they change up how you play. I so desperately wish there were ways to acquire different consultants over play. Now we get to the actual gameplay, trading. Now if this game had extremely high quality trading mechanics, it could probably make up for the lack of quality. But, it does not. During gameplay you can buy, sell or short, nothing else. While this might have been interesting on it's own if you could make decent assumptions about a baby's life, you simply can't. As far as I can tell, events that happen during a baby's life are totally random, with one or two being restricted to childhood. I've seen a person get married 3 times in a row (so over a period of maybe 6 years?) for example. Life events seem to have 0 impact on eachother, so you can't predict that someone getting married leads to a higher chance of having a kid because that's not how the game works. Similarly, even if a person goes through a series of unfortunate events, they're exactly as likely to try suicide as the guy with a wife, 2 kids and a good life. Oh but also, because events are pretty much specific to planets, some things like suicide aren't even possible on most planets because there isn't an event for it! Same goes for marriage, and such, basically many important life events can just, not happen on most planets. And even though the game has like 200-300 events, it doesn't feel that much because they're all spread on different planets. It's a very common occurance to have multiple repeat events per life, regularly. It doesn't end there though because next is balance! Other than the aforemention "playing as most characters feels awful because their unique gimmicks are all negative", the balance of the game is just off as well. There's no reason not to always bet on your first day, if you fail the bet, just start the campaign over. There's no reason not to immediatly ask the loan shark for money, if you lose everything, you're gonna restart anyway because there's no penalty for doing so. Once you reach your desired money goal, usually bronze if you don't care about score chasing like me, you have nothing to do the rest of the campaign and can just sit around in low stakes trading because risking your cash trading when you have what you need to progress is pointless. Some planets are also just definitely better than others. And some consultants are borderline useless too, and it's not like you can upgrade them or replace them with better consultants over time, you're just stuck with them. And that's all there is to the game. This entire review touches every single mechanic the game has, literally all of them, which is sadly very little. As a fellow developer I also hate to give negative reviews but I adored the previous game so much, and I could not recommend this game, and I feel so strongly about this I felt compelled to actually review it despite my reservations about doing so. I would love to see this game get a rework, move away from the mobile-style format of levels you need to complete to get stars/trophies, and into an actual campaign mode, hopefully with characters that aren't purely detriments to play and with more decisions to make, since as it stands the game feels very lacking in that department. TL;DR- fun for like 3 hours, barely any content, kinda mediocre gameplay, either wait for sales or better updates, just not worth 20 bucks at the moment long did read; got through the games content in about 5 hours, not necessarily a bad thing, but definitely a bad thing here. pretty barebones mechanics and half of the character's gimmicks are that they just dont have one of the three mechanics in the game it's kinda a roguelike but you can't really *do* anything to really change the run. when i saw in the stock limiter in the bottom right i expected to be able to pay money to upgrade it each run, sacrificing some important money early on for something that could greatly improve the run, but it just, stays the same each character same with the consultants, i expected them to change each day, but it stays the same for each character and is entirely scripted, why??? the consultants are pretty varied but not really, most of them are completely useless even in the best case scenario and some of them are seeing the average price of the baby, yknow like *the* thing that matters, like getting niche information from a consultant for a sidebet *is* interesting but is just not viable, i really tried to engage with the mechanic and it only paid off *once* by showing me one sidebet that would just fail, and thats it, again a choice between something that is useless 99.9% of the time, or to see the price of the thing you want to invest into, and again each character's consultants are the same so you just get to keep that guy the *entire* time, just feels pointless consultants take a % cut from the money that you are *going* to make, so theres no real reason not to take the really good consultants because you wouldnt have made that money anyways without them, so its just an automatic pick what i expected from the game was i would have had to invest money in consultants and keep investing money to make them more accurate, could have added opportunity cost, and might have made getting consultants for sidebets more viable, like if you could keep paying for more random events in the baby's life or pay more to narrow down the lifespan of a baby for multiple sidebets the character's each have their own storyline with scripted events on each day, this is fine in concept, being able to plan ahead on additional runs can be interesting, but in practice most of them are just losing money on certain days, which you really cant do much other than just make more money, which youre already trying to do so. the character's also just don't really have anything unique thats actually interesting, as an example one of the characters you play as is a corrupt politician that has power over the market that works through a proxy and you'd think that means you will be able to have access to manipulate the market and interesting stuff like that, but all it really means is you just buy and sell slow and that's it, its just really disappointing the shorting mechanic is really fun, and i love the theming of praying on a literal baby's downfall but there stops really being a reason to do it, its incredibly hard to balance finding time to short with full stocks, so you either do one or the other and wait on it, and since most babies values always go up its really hard to value in shorting it, and when you do get a successful short it is really isnt worth the risk sadly and consultants feel like they arent really built around the mechanic, again just disappointing it just feels like a game that gives you very little decisions to effect the run and little variation in the runs themselves im really glad they plan on updating this game though, i don't know if they'll fix most of the problems i have with it but im really glad it's getting popular at least but i still think its severely overpriced at the moment, i reccomend their other game in the series space warlord organ trading simulator if you havent tried it yet.

Space Warlord Baby Trading Simulator is a wild game that'll take you on an emotional rollercoaster and bring out the inner psycho in you in wanting the absolute worst happen to these virtual lives at the drop of a button. It is a dopamine hit of constant feedback and response as you want to squeeze out the most out of each trade and make that line keep going up. Its an overall enjoyable experience for getting through in an afternoon. Yet I feel that its still way overpriced for what its asking. Beyond simulated trading and making sidebets, the game doesn't ask any more of you or provide anymore beyond that. Campaigns modify the goals, but ultimately there is little to change up trades from day to day. The game is a very reactive experience, with a very minimal proactive experience in return. The game is still very worthwhile, but best worth getting during a sale rather than current price.

A great game held back by terrible performance. Playing a save file for too long seems to result in worse and worse lag. The game lags between loading screens, selecting babies, selecting planets, buying and selling, even just putting money into a side bet before the market actually opens causes lag. IDK why, perhaps its cause the game is generating the events for each baby or saving data, but even then the lag still seems far greater than what those operations would entail. In addition, there seems to be a bug with the daily scenario that prevents it from being playable the next day. After completing it the first time, I've checked every day for a week (for the achievement), and saw that it still said "come back tomorrow". This is a phenomenal game that I love but it really needs some optimization to not feel sluggish to play. I love the world and aesthetic of this and the first game, so I really hope this one gets some tweaks (as well as new scenarios) The music is really good though!

This is a hard game to recommend to anyone that doesn't understand the math that goes into speculative markets and finance. This is more of a puzzle game where you have to figure out on your own where your edges are and what information is actually valuable. It is also very much a push your luck game where your hubris ends up hurting in the long run. The game is pretty funny, but I do wish there was more to analyze or information to sink your teeth into.

I don't know what they're talking about, man. Woohoo Charlie comes in clutch. I learned a horrifying amount about speculative economics. It was a lot of fun. I also found myself staring out the window, depressed about the joke of our society, because very few things in this game is actually parody. Also, there's a lot of people here who say it's just completely random. It isn't, and they believe this because I imagine they gambled a mere one or two babies. You are given context clues by things like side bets (which even when they don't pay off are generally close) and information from consultants you can interpret and use to your advantage. Sure, you can also just gamble blindly, but even the cruelest scenarios don't give you NOTHING to work with.
